items.title: This man refused life-saving treatment because of his religion - days later the rules changed
items.summary: Jehovah's Witness leaders relaxed strict rules on blood transfusions, but the change came 23 days too late for Isaac Valdez.
items.content:
In August this year, 26-year-old Isaac Valdez had an epileptic seizure while browsing in his local library, causing him to convulse and strike his head against the ground.

He lost consciousness. Later, in hospital, it transpired Isaac had hit his head with such force it had led to a brain haemorrhage.

Treatment was seriously complicated by the fact that, as a Jehovah's Witness, Isaac carried a "No Blood" card, an indication that he would not accept treatment involving any form of blood transfusion because of his religious beliefs.

As a result, a procedure to drain fluid from Isaac's brain did not take place.

But his family, from Waxahachie, Texas, were encouraged by the fact that he regained consciousness and even started to talk again. He was able to confirm that he stood by his "no blood" beliefs.

The family's relief at his apparent improvement was short-lived. Isaac slipped into a coma and his condition worsened rapidly.

A neurosurgeon told Isaac's family the only way to save his life was an emergency operation, but that it was one that required blood transfusion.

His family took the decision to abide by Issac's wishes as a lifelong Witness not to accept such a procedure.

Isaac - who his twin brother Jacob Valdez describes as an intelligent man who loved volunteering and helping the elderly - died on 26 August 2026 when doctors turned off his life support.

Just 23 days later, the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body announced a seismic change in teaching that would, in effect, have given Isaac the religious green light to have the life-saving treatment he had refused.

The change suddenly means the vast majority of medical procedures using donated blood are no longer prohibited to followers. Now, decisions on whether to accept such treatments are to be left to individuals.

Jacob, already dealing with the death of his twin, was angered at the Jehovah's Witnesses' leadership for not coming to their conclusion sooner. He told BBC News he believes Isaac could well still be alive if they had.

The original rule on blood transfusions dates back to 1945, towards the very end of a war during which the use of blood transfusions had been increasingly widespread. The leaders of Jehovah's Witnesses announced that their believers were not permitted to accept transfusions.

This was based on their interpretation of Bible verses from both the Old and New Testaments prohibiting the consumption of blood, including one from the Book of Acts that instructs believers to abstain from blood, from food offered to idols, and from things that had been strangled.

So, why has the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body, based in New York state, now decided to change the rules, 81 years after introducing them?

It comes after years of pressure from both within and outside the faith, but that is not how leaders of the faith describe the decision.

"The change is basically the application of Bible principles to modern medicine and its methods," says the Jehovah's Witnesses international spokesperson, Paul Gillies, who described it as both a fresh look at scripture and at medical advances.

We meet Gillies at the Jehovah's Witnesses UK headquarters set in 85 acres of Essex countryside. It is a vast modern complex where hundreds of volunteer followers of the faith live and work without pay.

He insists the basic teaching has not changed and that the transfusion of whole blood is still prohibited. However, for decades, most transfusions have not used whole blood, instead using the specific components of blood that are needed by the patient.

The change is being justified by permitting the use of blood components, like plasma and red blood cells and platelets, in the huge numbers of medical procedures that were previously banned.

Gillies says the Bible references "abstaining from blood" but not "various components that could be extracted from blood".

He says the Governing Body felt it their duty to avoid scriptural "overreach" and only apply what was specifically described in the Bible.

But that explanation has stunned many and led them to ask if it was not a huge overreach 81 years ago to ban blood transfusions in the first place, when transfusions are not specifically mentioned in the bible.

Others are then also asking why it has taken so long to come to this landmark decision, given that transfusions that do not use whole blood have been the norm for decades.

These are questions Jacob asked as soon as the ban was lifted, just days after a memorial service for Isaac.

Jacob, who had already left the Jehovah's Witness faith he was brought up in, texted prominent figures from Isaac's congregation in Texas after Isaac's death. The messages are full of angst, and painful to read.

He asked them to consider "the part you played in encouraging so many people to sacrifice their life for something that was never God's will".

Most did not reply, but one "elder" responded saying he could not understand why Jacob was so angry and fixated on the policy shift.

This all further infuriated Jacob, who particularly wants the faith's decision-makers to be accountable for all the lives lost.

"I want to ask them if they could apologise directly, I would like not to have a deflected answer, just straightforward apology," he says.

It is extremely difficult to say how many Jehovah's Witnesses, among the estimated nine million followers of the faith worldwide, died each year having refused treatment involving blood transfusions. But research in one medical journal in 2016, The Obstetrical & Gynecological Survey, put the figure at around 1,100.

"We're sympathetic to their feelings, and if individuals have lost family members and are concerned about some of these questions, they deserve to be heard compassionately," says Gillies.

But there was little clarity about why the change did not come earlier.

"Why has it taken this time? Well, I guess because it takes time, it doesn't necessarily mean that there is some magic change that's taken place," says Gillies.

And when asked, Gillies deflects calls for the leadership to apologise, saying that many lives had, in fact, been saved because faithful Jehovah's Witnesses had not been exposed to blood contamination scandals.

He also insists that even after the new edict, some Jehovah's Witnesses could still decide they did not want to accept a transfusion, and that may have been the case even if the edict had come years ago.

Indeed, the BBC spoke with Alex Ball, 58, a Jehovah's Witness from West Sussex, who says in 2012 a doctor told him he would not survive the chemotherapy he needed to treat his blood cancer unless he also had a transfusion.

"I wanted to adhere as closely to the scriptures as possible when I was sick, and I think I did that well."

With help from what is called "a Jehovah's Witness Hospital Liaison Committee", Alex found an American consultant who could perform a treatment to boost Alex's blood cells without the need for any products from someone else. His UK consultant agreed to treat him using the new method and it worked.

More than a decade later, Alex says he would make the same decision again, despite the change in blood policy that would have permitted the transfusions he had been told he needed.

Elisha Cummings, 50, a Jehovah's Witness from Trinidad and Tobago, was unable to donate blood to her aunt, who died, because of the rules.

They also cost her her marriage too, with her husband of 10 years leaving the faith and divorcing her after it came to light that he had had a blood transfusion as a child, something that was looked down upon in her Witness community.

"Since the blood policy change, I have not been myself," she says. "It left me in a sort of depressed mode."

"How many houses did I go to trying to convince people about the blood doctrine? And you're coming now and it's something totally different," Elisha says.

Elisha says her beliefs as a whole have been shaken, yet she feels reluctant to leave the faith, partly because it is what provides her with her community and she fears isolation.

In the past, those who disagreed with "blood doctrine" were ostracised or felt like they needed to leave the faith. Will they now be able to come back?

"Any individual that wants to come back to the faith is warmly welcomed," says Gillies, speaking of those who had left the faith because they had accepted a transfusion for themselves or a relative.

"If they would like to become one of Jehovah's Witnesses again and would like to speak to the elders, then they're very welcome to do so."

items.title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu
items.summary: For some tourists, the contrast between Somalia's reputation and what they experience on the ground can be striking.
items.content:
As the sun rises over the Indian Ocean, waves lap onto the golden sands while palm fronds rustle in the cool sea breeze. Welcome to... Mogadishu.

This is the image that one young Somali woman wants the world to have of her home city - in contrast to the one of suicide attacks and young men wielding AK-47s that many people currently associate with Somalia's capital.

Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader is among a growing number of local guides taking visitors beyond the headlines to explore Mogadishu's beauty spots, historic sites and culture.

Her favourite spot is Jazeera beach, where visitors can enjoy the sea before heading to nearby sand dunes.

"It's one of the tourist attractions where we bring our guests. It's a nice place," says the 23-year-old.

But her tours are about more than scenic views. She also takes visitors to the fish market, where they discover the variety of marine life available along Somalia's extensive coastline and to parts of the city that reflect its history as a busy Indian Ocean trading centre, with the influences of both its Ottoman and Italian former rulers.

Visitors can also sample Somali food, including camel meat, samosas and traditional tea.

Sucdi says many arrive in the city with expectations shaped by years of hearing about the insecurity.

"Mostly, they are surprised by how beautiful the country is and how welcoming people are," she says.

At the fish market, she says, visitors are particularly impressed by the variety of fish species.

Guiding tours runs in Sucdi's family. Her father worked in the profession for over three decades, taking journalists, photographers and visitors from different countries around Somalia.

"I started this job as a hobby, but it has become something that I like and am passionate about," she says.

She now works alongside her father and a team of guides, building on his experience while using social media to reach a wider audience.

She shares videos of her tours on TikTok, offering people outside Somalia a glimpse of places they may never have imagined visiting.

She is also considering producing content in English to reach audiences who do not speak Somali.

Tourism remains a relatively new field in Somalia, she says, with only a handful working as guides in Mogadishu.

The business is seasonal, but Sucdi says this year has been particularly encouraging, although numbers are still fairly low. Having five tourists a week is considered a success but she is confident that numbers will grow.

However, she says many visitors are still concerned about security.

Since the collapse of Somalia's central government in 1991, Mogadishu has endured decades of civil war, destruction and displacement. Much of the city centre was reduced to rubble, and basic services and infrastructure largely broke down.

But following the withdrawal of the Islamist militant group al-Shabab from most of the city in 2011, and the establishment of the federal government in 2012, Mogadishu has undergone a gradual transformation.

Returning members of the Somali diaspora, local entrepreneurs and investors helped fuel a construction boom, with new hotels, restaurants, businesses and residential developments reshaping the capital.

Today, Mogadishu is a growing commercial hub, although insecurity and the legacy of conflict remain part of everyday life.

About 10,000 tourists visited Somalia in 2024, a 50% increase on the previous year, according to the country's tourism department.

Many visitors ask about their safety before travelling and often encounter security checkpoints around the city.

But she says their experience on the ground is generally positive.

"What they heard from the news and everywhere else is not the same as what they see in the country," she says.

Although some question whether Mogadishu is safe enough for a young woman to be working as a tour guide, Sucdi is determined to continue.

She wants visitors to experience a Somalia that is rarely seen.

"I would want them to see the beautiful, welcoming side of Mogadishu, and not the side that they heard from the media, which is explosions and bombs," she says.

Somalia has Africa's longest mainland coastline, stretching more than 3,000km (1,860 miles) along the Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden.

Its beaches and sand dunes sit alongside historic coastal cities such as Mogadishu, whose culture reflects centuries of Indian Ocean trade.

For some tourists, that contrast between the country's reputation and what they experience can be striking.

American travel content creator Chris Reese, who goes by the name Authentic Travelling, has visited Mogadishu twice.

His first trip, almost a year ago, was a solo visit. He enjoyed it so much that he decided to return with a group of friends, who had seen videos of his visit on social media.

"I had such a positive experience - I really enjoyed seeing the country for the first time - that I opted to bring back a group of my friends," he says.

What stands out for Chris is the city's coastal setting, its food and atmosphere.

"It is such a beautiful tropical place. I love the vibe, the weather and the food," he says.

During the group's visit, they enjoy lunch overlooking the Indian Ocean before heading out to explore the beaches and sand dunes.

"The desert is beautiful and picturesque. It is also amazing that it's barely a 30-minute drive from Mogadishu," he says.

Before his first trip, Chris says, much of what he knew about Somalia came from international news coverage.

"If you only read the news reports about Somalia, you would be scared to visit. And honestly, that's what I saw in the media before I came, mostly negative headlines."

"Coming here, on my very first trip, showed me that there is so much more to this country than what is shown in the headlines," he says.

Mihaela Patap, from Romania, loves Somalia's natural beauty.

Although she has spent only a few hours in Mogadishu, she has already visited the sand dunes and taken in the Indian Ocean coastline.

"The desert was so beautiful to see. I have also enjoyed the beach, and the ocean. It is inspiring," she says.

Having travelled to Somalia from neighbouring Ethiopia, she says she has been struck by the people's friendliness.

"I don't see anything dangerous. I feel safe and the people are warm," she says.

An experienced traveller, Mihaela says she prefers to visit new countries without having preconceived ideas.

"I travel the world to see new places, to see countries, to see the differences. I don't take a picture in my mind to compare the reality with. I'm just expecting the new to come to me," she says.

She hopes to share her experience and encourage others to visit Somalia.

"I'm going to post my pictures and say good things about what I'm experiencing. I'm going to promote it," she says.

She is continuing a family profession while building a business in an industry with few women and using digital platforms to reach audiences far beyond Mogadishu.

"Somalia still has a long way to go before tourism becomes a major industry," she says.

"Through my tours, I am giving visitors an opportunity to experience its landscapes, our culture and people beyond the familiar negative headlines."

For her, every visitor is another opportunity to tell a fuller story of Mogadishu.

items.title: Samsung Secrets: i Samsung AI TV si trasformano in una console di ultima generazione, serve solo un controller
items.summary: Il Gaming Hub di Samsung nasconde un vero PC da gaming all'interno del televisore. Ecco cosa serve per giocare in 4K a 60 fps (e oltre) direttamente dal cloud ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Quando si pensa di acquistare una nuova console da gioco o un PC per il gaming in 4K, ci sono sempre più ostacoli: hardware introvabile e prezzi fuori controllo. Eppure, se in salotto c’è un televisore Samsung AI TV, quella “console” è già pronta all'uso e non ha bisogno di alcuna “scatola" aggiuntiva posizionata sotto lo schermo. Si chiama Samsung Gaming Hub ed è uno degli elementi più potenti — e spesso meno esplorati — della piattaforma Smart TV Tizen. Non è una semplice raccolta di app, ma un ambiente che trasforma il TV in una stazione da gioco di alto livello, azzerando la necessità di acquistare hardware dedicato.

Il principio alla base del Gaming Hub è semplice: l'elaborazione grafica non avviene sul televisore, ma su server remoti ad altissime prestazioni. Il TV riceve un flusso video a bassissima latenza e invia i comandi impartiti dal controller.

A differenza di qualche anno fa, la maturità delle piattaforme di cloud gaming di oggi garantisce una qualità sovrapponibile a quella di una macchina fisica di altissimo livello , e i Samsung AI TV supportano i migliori servizi oggi disponibili per qualità e titoli disponibili:

Dal Gaming Hub puoi sfogliare direttamente il catalogo aggregato dei titoli disponibili, ricevere raccomandazione dei giochi che ti possono interessare, con indicazione chiara dei servizi di cloud gaming in cui li puoi trovare. Basta selezionare il gioco, la piattaforma e sei pronto a iniziare.

Accedere a centinaia di titoli con il Gaming Hub è più semplice di quello che credi: basta collegare un controller. Il Gaming Hub abbatte qualsiasi barriera perché non richiede un gamepad proprietario : Samsung AI TV supportano infatti i principali controller per console e Bluetooth: c’è la compatibilità nativa via Bluetooth o USB via cavo per i controller Xbox, Xbox Elite, PlayStation DualSense e DualShock 4, Amazon Luna.

Come si collega? Dalla schermata principale del Gaming Hub, basta selezionare l'icona del controller per avviare la ricerca Bluetooth ed effettuare l'abbinamento in pochi secondi. Collegando un cavo USB a una porta del TV o del box One Connect, il riconoscimento è immediato e plug-and-play.

E se sei un amante dei giochi in prima persona e non ami il controller da gioco non c’è nessun problema. Puoi anche collegare mouse e tastiera , sia via Bluetooth che tramite le porte USB, e giocare esattamente come da PC. E siccome anche l’audio è importante, con i Samsung AI TV puoi collegare direttamente anche cuffie e auricolari Bluetooth, con gestione dell'audio a 360° e modalità a bassa latenza.

Se invece possiedi già un PC da gaming rig o una console di ultima generazione (come PS5 o Xbox Series X), il Gaming Hub si trasforma nel centro di controllo per le sorgenti esterne via HDMI 2.1. I Samsung AI TV sono equipaggiati di quattro ingressi HDMI 2.1 completi che offrono accesso a tutte le funzionalità aggiuntive dello standard pensate per il gaming.

Collegando un PC da gaming, i modelli Micro RGB, Neo QLED e OLED Samsung più recenti spingono il refresh rate oltre lo standard dei 120 Hz, raggiungendo perfino i 165 Hz , garantendo la fluidità e l’input lag tipici dei monitor da eSports. Grazie al supporto nativo per VRR (Variable Refresh Rate), AMD FreeSync Premium Pro e, sulla gamma OLED, alla compatibilità NVIDIA G-Sync, lo schermo del TV adatta in tempo reale la sua frequenza ai framerate del PC o della console, azzerando tearing e micro-scatti per una schermata di gioco sempre incredibilmente fluida.

Grazie alla funzione ALLM (bassa latenza automatica), i Samsung AI TV riconoscono automaticamente la console o il PC e impostano automaticamente la modalità gioco. Grazie all’IA, il TV riconosce il tipo di gioco e ottimizza automaticamente l’immagine per garantire la resa migliore in base al genere. Premendo l'apposito tasto sul telecomando si richiama poi la Game Bar, un menù dedicato che consente di visualizzare in tempo reale il frame e di accedere rapidamente a tutte le funzioni di gioco. Tra le ultime novità troviamo la funzione MiniMap Auto Detect che sfrutta l’intelligenza artificiale per riconoscere la mini mappa di gioco e la ingrandisce in un riquadro dedicato. Il Virtual Aim Point sovrappone invece un mirino virtuale su schermo per aiutarti ad ottenere maggiore precisione negli sparatutto in prima persona.

items.title: Allarmi bomba sugli aerei, un’altra giornata di caos. Meloni: “siamo preoccupati”
items.summary: Segnalazioni in tutto il continente, tre in Italia. Evacuate le sedi di media in Irlanda e Bulgaria. La rivendicazione: “È solo l’inizio”
items.content:
Era attesa e puntuale è arrivata. Per il secondo giorno consecutivo un’ondata di falsi allarmi bomba ha scatenato il caos nei cieli europei, con voli dirottati, scortati dai caccia e bonificati all’arrivo, proprio mentre una serie di false segnalazioni venivano recapitate alle redazioni di una ventina di media tra Irlanda, Gran Bretagna e Bulgaria.

Le intelligence se lo aspettavano, anzi — si ragiona — in un certo senso non avrebbe potuto essere altrimenti. Una campagna di swatting — così si chiama in gergo — non necessita di grandi risorse. Per inviare una valanga di falsi allarmi relativi a obiettivi sensibili, bastano una serie di account trafugati o anonimizzati — sono diversi i provider che li forniscono — e connessioni private o cifrate che schermano l’origine del traffico telematico o telefonico. Quelle individuate con i primi approfondimenti sono di livello avanzato, ma perché uno swatting sia efficace non è neanche necessario. E il risulto è massimo: servizi di sicurezza mobilitati, danni economici, ma soprattutto panico e disorientamento nella popolazione .

Un fenomeno che le intelligence monitorano da tempo con preoccupazione: gli attacchi aumentano a ritmo vertiginoso. Solo nell’ultimo anno, afferma il Dipartimento di sicurezza, quelli sulle scuole Usa sono aumentati del 540%. Protocolli per identificare la natura dei messaggi, form che identifichino utenti sospetti e filtri esistono e sopra ci si lavora, ma in caso di obiettivi sensibili la prudenza è d’obbligo.

Ecco perché alla fine dell’ennesima giornata di falsi allarmi, si possono solo fare i conti. Con 9 voli monitorati Praga è stato lo scalo messo più sotto stress, altri quattro su Madrid, due in Italia, altri ancora a Bruxelles, Parigi e Sofia. In tutto sono almeno 22, che si aggiungono ai 25 aerei disturbati da falsi allarmi bomba il giorno prima, ai sette del 2 novembre, come all’unica segnalazione dell’1 novembre, in un mese complicato da attacchi ai sistemi di refrigerazione in tutta Europa e ondate di falsi allarmi nelle scuole di Italia, Serbia, Scozia, Irlanda del Nord e Ungheria. Al caos nei cieli, ieri si è aggiunto il tentativo di mettere a soqquadro i media, con almeno una decina fra radio, tv e giornali irlandesi evacuati e bonificati.

Che si tratti di un’evoluzione “dell’attacco” al settore aereo del giorno precedente lo dichiara in una mail recapitata a diversi media irlandesi, britannici e bulgari il sedicente capo dell’organizzazione neonazista russa Male Legion che aveva rivendicato i primi attacchi. «Questo è solo l’inizio. Molto presto faremo saltare in aria i vostri aerei, navi da crociera, stazioni della metropolitana e treni», promette Mikhail Andropov . Un nome, fanno notare gli analisti, che evoca quello dello storico capo del Kgb poi diventato capo del partito, ma di cui non sembra esserci traccia sui canali ancora attivi del movimento. Esattamente gli stessi su cui il fondatore, Vladislav Pozdnyakov , smentisce qualsiasi coinvolgimento dell’organizzazione: «Non c’è più».

Tutti elementi da prendere con le pinze suggeriscono analisti e investigatori, sempre più inclini a leggere un disegno e una strategia unica nello sciame di allarmi e attacchi, ma probabilmente attori diversi e non in contrasto fra loro. «Per adesso però — spiega una fonte vicina al fascicolo — non ci sono elementi concreti». La prossima settimana a Bruxelles si riuniranno gli esperti della sicurezza aerea dei 27 Paesi per discutere le misure di risposta e prevenzione necessarie, ma al momento, conferma la commissione Ue ai Trasporti, «tocca alle autorità nazionali procedere». In Italia le procure di Milano, Busto Arsizio e Roma procedono per procurato allarme, ma è lavoro che anche la Direzione nazionale antimafia e antiterrorismo segue da vicino. Diverso il discorso per l’attacco hacker ai refrigeratori: il procuratore nazionale Giovanni Melillo ha deciso di assumere il coordinamento delle indagini degli uffici interessati.

L’ondata di attacchi hacker e falsi allarmi «dice che sotto attacco sono le infrastrut ture civili», afferma una preoccupata premier Meloni, mentre il ministro degli Esteri spagnolo Albares parla di «tentativo di aggressione ibrida e di guerra psicologica». Intanto in Europa cresce la preoccupazione per i vertici che giovedì e venerdì riuniranno a Dublino almeno 50 leader dell’Ue. «Si stanno mettendo a punto adeguati protocolli di risposta», assicura il premier Michael Martin. Ma il percorso per individuare l’origine della minaccia sembra invece tutto in salita.

items.title: Cornell faculty pass no-confidence vote over leadership's handling of Jane Doe allegations
items.summary: Friday's resolution by academic staff is largely symbolic as they do not have the power to remove those in charge of the university.
items.content:
Cornell University's academic staff have passed a vote of no confidence over its leadership's handling of what staff call a "crisis of sexual assault" after a former student alleged she was gang raped while attending.

The woman, known anonymously as Jane Doe, is suing her former university and the fraternity over an alleged incident involving several men at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024.

All seven of the accused have denied wrongdoing when contacted by the BBC's US partner CBS. None has been charged with a crime.

Friday's no-confidence vote passed by 75 votes to 50. It is largely symbolic because the faculty senate does not have the power to remove leaders.

The resolution states that the faculty senate, which represents academic staff, "has no confidence in the ability of the central administration to effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault at Cornell University".

It did not make any specific recommendations or suggest what administrators did wrong in response to the accusation.

It is a rebuke of university leaders including President Michael Kotlikoff, whom Doe has accused of asking why she waited several weeks to report the incident.

The Ivy League institution in upstate New York has said her account of Kotlikoff's reaction is "incorrect".

Doe's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, responded to the vote's outcome in a statement, saying: "We recently learned that Cornell's Faculty Senate made a finding of no confidence in the Central Administration's ability to address the longstanding crisis of sexual assault at Cornell.

"We believe that the Faculty Senate did not reach this decision lightly and considered all available information."

Giuffra added: "We are hopeful that this will be yet another step forward to educate and support the Cornell community by addressing the longstanding scourge of sexual assault on campus."

The board of trustees, which does have the power to fire Kotlikoff, said in a statement that it "remains confident" that he and his administration "are the right leaders to thoughtfully and comprehensively address the serious problem of sexual assault on our campus".

Trustees board chairwoman Anne Meinig Smalling, added: "This confidence is rooted not only in the administration's actions to date and plans moving forward, but also in its track record of navigating complex problems."

She also said that the vote of no confidence "reflects the deep anger across our campus and sends a clear signal that what happened to Jane Doe is unacceptable".

Backlash against Cornell has been intense since Doe filed her lawsuit in September. She reported the alleged assault to campus police after it happened but the local prosecutor declined to bring charges at the time.

Cornell, after initially defending its disciplinary measures, has acknowledged it fell short in its handling of her case and has hired a former attorney general to conduct an independent review of the case. It also recently announced a series of measures due assault, including cancelling fraternity parties.

New York state prosecutors, led by Attorney General Letitia James, are carrying out their own investigation to decide if criminal charges are warranted.

Earlier this week, New York Governor Kathy Hochul announced that state police would investigate any future sexual offence complaints at the university.

items.title: Libghostty 1.0
items.summary: Article URL: https://mitchellh.com/writing/libghostty-1-0 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50399933 Points: 852 # Comments: 140
items.content:
libghostty-vt 1.0 is here. libghostty is a portable, high-performance C library for terminal emulation, extracted directly from the core of Ghostty. The 1.0 release means both the library itself and the C ABI are now stable.

A little over a year ago, I wrote that libghostty is coming . At the time, the Zig module had just been merged, the C API didn't exist, and nobody but Ghostty was a consumer. Today, the C API is a complete terminal emulator, it runs in production for millions of people across hundreds of products, both free and commercial, and it has a real, enforced ABI stability policy.

This post is about how we got here and what 1.0 actually means. 1

Since starting the Ghostty project in 2022, the most common question I've been asked is "why?". I already answered this in the libghostty is coming post, so feel free to read that if you wish. Today, I'd rather answer this by showing the broad industry impact libghostty has already had . I believe this strongly validates its existence.

A year ago, I used a bug in JediTerm , the terminal emulator in JetBrains IDEs, as an example of why terminal emulation is hard to get right. A year later, the terminal in JetBrains IDEs now runs on libghostty . Every IntelliJ, PyCharm, GoLand, etc. user now has a libghostty-powered terminal. Based on a report by JetBrains, that's over 12.5 million active users.

Neovim has an approved pull request replacing libvterm with libghostty-vt . Among other things, it closes a 10-year-old issue about reflowing scrollback on resize. The maintainers are waiting on a tagged release before merging so that distributions can package the dependency separately, and the release today should enable that.

KDE developers are experimenting with a Konsole replacement built on it. Vercel's Turborepo uses it to render task output in its TUI. devenv uses it to drive shells. Antithesis used it to fuzz TUI programs and found real bugs in btop and others. Ghostel brings it to Emacs. ghostty-web is the WASM build with an Xterm.js-compatible API. Commercial products like OrbStack embed it. And a whole wave of new terminals and "agentic" coding tools, such as herdr and cmux , have been built on it rather than writing yet another emulator.

There are community bindings for Rust, Go, JavaScript, Swift, Python, .NET, Elixir, Dart, Java, and more, and the awesome-libghostty list tracks well over a hundred projects.

More people today use a terminal powered by libghostty than use Ghostty the application, by a very large multiple. And libghostty is having a much larger impact than being "just" a terminal emulator. 2

1.0 means libghostty-vt follows semantic versioning and has strict ABI compatibility promises so that packagers across distributions and operating systems can be confident packaging libghostty-vt and program developers can be confident dynamically linking against it.

Beyond providing useful features, I believe the hallmark of a high-quality and enduring C library is ABI stability. So from the start, I took inspiration from C libraries I enjoyed working with and designed the API to have a strong, stable ABI that allows for future additions.

Every object is an opaque handle. The hundreds of values you might read or write go through a small set of enum-keyed getters and setters, so we can add new values easily without introducing a new symbol. Programs with newer headers linked against an older libghostty get GHOSTTY_UNSUPPORTED results instead of crashes or undefined behavior. The few non-opaque structs we have carry their size so that fields can be appended later, or contain reserved padding. Enums are pinned to int on every compiler, as much as the C standard allows.

Our CI enforces our ABI policy. Every change is checked with libabigail against a committed baseline on Linux, and against golden type manifests on macOS and WebAssembly.

On ELF platforms, every exported symbol is also versioned, so the dynamic loader refuses to load a mismatched library by name rather than failing in some mysterious way later.

In addition to ABI stability, the 1.0 release brings along the proper build tooling, tarballs, dependency licensing manifests, documentation, and more to enable every major operating system and distribution to package libghostty-vt through standard official tooling.

Libghostty has its own release cycle, separate from Ghostty the application. And it has its own tarballs with only the files and dependencies libghostty needs, resulting in smaller sizes and simpler licensing verification and compatibility.

Each release publishes a signed source tarball along with a companion dependencies tarball containing every Zig package in Zig's own cache layout, so a distribution can build the library completely offline. The build installs the shared and static libraries with a proper SONAME, headers, pkg-config files, and a CMake package config, and it honors --prefix , DESTDIR , and lib64 . Debug info is kept by default so distros can split it out. All of this is documented in PACKAGING-LIBGHOSTTY.md , which ships with the tarball.

libghostty-vt is MIT licensed. At runtime it needs nothing beyond libc, and it can be built fully freestanding if you don't want that either. 3

The library compiles in a small number of permissively licensed dependencies: simdutf and Google Highway for SIMD, a compact Unicode table for grapheme data, and Wuffs for image decoding in the Kitty graphics protocol. Both simdutf and Highway are built without libc++ , so there is no C++ standard library dependency.

There is no copyleft code anywhere in the dependency tree. Every dependency is listed in a machine-readable manifest with its version, SPDX license, and hash, specifically so distros can fill in their bundled-library metadata more easily.

If a distro would rather dynamically link the system simdutf or Highway, there's a build flag for that.

libghostty-vt is highly portable. The table below lists all the platforms and architectures that we build and test (full unit tests plus running all examples) in CI:

There is a second set of platforms we build in CI but do not run tests for. These systems all have known users; we just haven't set up the machinery for automated testing:

Portability isn't just about the ability to build and run. It's also about resource usage and being able to work in a wide variety of resource environments.

For resource usage, the library creates no threads, allocates only through an allocator you can customize, and uses minimal compute and memory. I've run 10,000 active terminals, each with a live shell producing output, on a Linux server with 4 cores and 8 GB of RAM. In this test, I had to use dash because bash used far more RAM than libghostty-vt and wouldn't fit into the 8 GB budget.

You can now create a terminal in ~1,500 lines of C that has more features and better performance than just about any terminal that existed in 2025, and most today in 2026. 5 And thanks to the rich ecosystem of language bindings, you can do this in every major programming language. You get this for free. For almost no effort. You can just do it.

libghostty-vt is a generalized library, so we will focus on stability while implementing as many terminal protocols as exist (giving options to enable/disable them, of course) so that embedders have the luxury of choice.

Every bug any libghostty-vt embedder reports makes everyone else in the ecosystem better. Every feature we ship in libghostty-vt becomes available to everyone quickly and safely. Terminals can move faster with less fragmentation.

Thank you to everyone who contributed to the library, wrote bindings, filed bugs, and shipped something on top of it while the API was still experimental. As with all open source, this was the work of a large community.

As usual, I hate that I have to do this for every post, but I want to note this post was completely hand-written with no AI assistance. ↩

The numbers are rough because most consumers don't report usage, but JetBrains alone reports 12.5 million recurring active users , and that's before counting everything else on the list. ↩

In the original post I wrote "not even libc!" The default build does link libc, because the SIMD paths use it and the default allocator is malloc . Turn off SIMD and the library is freestanding, which is how it runs on bare-metal RISC-V and ARM targets. ↩

The feature flags aren't WASM-specific; they work on every target. They're likely useful for things like embedded devices too. ↩

"Features" here means the set of terminal protocols and sequences understood, and "performance" means parsing throughput and memory usage, since those are the parts libghostty-vt provides. ↩

items.title: With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle
items.summary: The US president's promotion of Miller, a loyal partisan firebrand to be his new chief of staff sets up likely clashes with Congress.
items.content:
In the aftermath of the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, Donald Trump said he would be willing to work with the newly ascendent Democrats in Congress.

On Friday, however, he elevated Stephen Miller, his bare-knuckled political operative and longtime adviser, to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.

Far from an olive branch to Congress, Miller's promotion could be a sign that the president is girding for political battle by installing a partisan firebrand in the top White House job.

"The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our president and defend this magnificent republic," Miller posted on X, adding that he was "honored beyond words" to be Trump's pick for the job.

One of the most powerful positions in Washington, the chief of staff is gatekeeper to the president, agenda-setter in the White House and chief negotiator with Congress and other outside political interests.

"Stephen Miller's been with me since the beginning," Trump said in comments to reporters after announcing the move on his Truth Social website. "He gets it."

Miller is best known for being the driving force behind the Trump administration's aggressive immigration enforcement policies, which has included ramping up funding for enforcement operations across the US.

He made headlines when he called Alex Pretti, who was shot and killed by federal immigration officials during a massive deportation operation in Minneapolis, a "domestic terrorist" and an "assassin". He would later walk back those words, saying federal agents "may not have been following" proper protocol.

He has also reportedly played a leading role in the US military operations in Venezuela and against suspected drug trafficking operations in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, which critics have condemned as extra-judicial killings.

Miller joined Trump's political operation early in his 2016 presidential bid as a strategist and incendiary warm-up speaker at his raucous campaign rallies.

He was one of the few senior White House staffers to persevere through the entirety of his first term. He stayed loyal to Trump during his political exile following attempts to overturn his ballot-box defeat in 2020 failed. He then returned in the influential role of deputy chief of staff for policy in Trump's second term.

Wiles, who co-managed the president's successful 2024 re-election campaign, developed a reputation as a cool professional who avoided the White House staffing upheavals, dramatic policy reversals and personality clashes that typified Trump's first presidential term.

The president, however, began souring on Wiles in recent months, as his political standing in the US declined, culminating in Tuesday's electoral rout. He also reportedly chafed at news stories indicating that those in Wiles' orbit were landing lucrative consulting jobs through their connections to the president.

Trump names Stephen Miller as new White House chief of staff

'Trump's psyche': The aide driving president's most controversial policies

While Trump praised Miller's effectiveness as a manager on Friday, working with Congress could prove to be a challenge.

It is difficult to overstate how disliked Miller is by most Democrats – and some Republicans.

"Stephen Miller is a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands," Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries wrote on X. "His presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor."

Earlier this year, Miller posted on social media that James Talarico, who had just secured the Democratic nomination to run for Senate in Texas, was "their first transgender Senate candidate".

The Democratic Party offered a terse, obscenity laced reply, telling Miller to shut up.

Now Miller will have to negotiate with a US Senate that includes a newly elected Talarico as one of its rising stars, after an election in which polls found that 58% of voters believe the administration's immigration enforcement actions had "gone too far" and Hispanics decisively turned against Republican candidates.

On Wednesday, in a social media post attempting to explain the Republican midterm defeats, Vice-President JD Vance - who is an early frontrunner for the Republican 2028 presidential nomination - wrote that he was "open to the idea that we should change enforcement - by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labour, for instance".

That now seems less likely with an immigration hardline taking the White House helm.

Thom Tillis, the North Carolina Republican senator who is retiring at the end of the year, has been particularly vocal in condemning Miller. He has called him "incompetent" and "the architect of some of the dumbest proposals from the Trump White House".

"Stephen Miller has been a true conservative warrior since his days as a Senate staffer, a staunch defender of law and order against illegal invasions and leftist lawlessness, and a steadfast fighter for President Trump for over a decade," Utah Senator Mike Lee posted on X after Trump's announcement.

At a time when congressional Democrats are promising to launch new investigations and oversight into the Trump administration, it appears that a "warrior" and a "fighter" is the kind of person the president wants to have running his White House.

White House denies Hegseth and Rubio to leave jobs after Republican election losses

Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here . Those outside the UK can sign up here .

items.title: Il presidente del Paraguay Santiago Peña è stato destituito e arrestato
items.summary: Era sotto impeachment per uno scandalo che riguarda una delle banche più importanti del paese, la Ueno Bank
items.content:
Il presidente di destra del Paraguay Santiago Peña è stato rimosso dal suo incarico: dopo la Camera, anche il Senato ha votato all’unanimità per la sua destituzione. La procura ha disposto per lui gli arresti domiciliari per violazione della fiducia e altri reati. Peña era sotto impeachment per via di uno scandalo bancario e di un’indagine che riguardano la Ueno Bank, una banca digitale fondata nel 2021 e diventata una delle più importanti del paese, a cui Peña è legato.

Martedì la Banca centrale del Paraguay aveva detto che la Ueno Bank si trovava in una situazione finanziaria molto rischiosa, al limite del dissesto. L’aveva quindi messa sotto sequestro e aveva avviato una procedura di risoluzione, bloccando temporaneamente tutti i conti correnti e impedendo ai suoi 3 milioni di clienti di accedere ai loro risparmi o di fare operazioni online: un problema enorme. Secondo la Banca centrale il coefficiente di solvibilità di Ueno Bank, un indicatore del rapporto tra il capitale di cui la banca dispone e i suoi debiti, era meno di metà del minimo legale.

La banca ha estesi legami con la classe politica del Paraguay. È accusata di aver concesso prestiti eccessivi e poco trasparenti a società legate ai soci del Grupo Vázquez, il conglomerato proprietario di Ueno Bank, di cui fino al marzo del 2025 era azionista anche Peña. Martedì le autorità paraguaiane hanno disposto l’arresto di otto persone, fra cui il presidente e l’amministratore delegato.

Peña è un politico conservatore molto vicino all’amministrazione del presidente statunitense Donald Trump. È il leader del Partito Colorado , che governa il Paraguay quasi ininterrottamente dal 1947. Negli ultimi giorni aveva cercato di non farsi coinvolgere dallo scandalo e aveva chiesto le dimissioni del presidente della Banca centrale, Carlos Carvallo, a cui però lui stesso aveva dato l’incarico.

Giovedì Peña si era dimesso da presidente, ma il Congresso non aveva formalizzato le sue dimissioni, altrimenti sarebbe diventato senatore a vita e avrebbe goduto dell’immunità parlamentare, votando parallelamente per metterlo sotto impeachment.

items.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
items.summary: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.
items.content:
Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have recovered slightly from an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index closed in positive territory following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday.

Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development.

However the latest US employment figures added to a mixed picture for American markets on Friday morning, with an unexpectedly strong 165,000 jobs added to the economy in September.

On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers.

But the Nasdaq Composite bounced back slightly on Friday, ending the day up 1.1%, partly reversing some of its 5.5% fall.

The S&P 500, which tracks the share prices of the largest publicly-traded US companies, closed up 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was flat through the day before ending slightly down 0.4%.

Companies that lost hundreds of billions in market value recovered some ground on Friday, including Nvidia, SpaceX and Tesla.

The Kospi in South Korea closed down 6% on Friday, with shares in chipmaker SK Hynix plunging more than 10%. European markets also fell, with the main indexes in Germany, France and Spain ending the day down.

In the UK, the FTSE 100, which tracks the largest companies on the London Stock Exchange, declined 1.01%.

In addition to the recent market volatility, UK traders were also digesting the latest Bank of England decision to raise interest rates and the signal that another rate rise could be on the cards to curb rising prices.

The market fluctuations also come after the sweeping Democrat victory in the midterm elections.

A number of Democrats campaigned for new rules and regulations for artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres, and the party has since won control of both houses of congress as well as key contests in states that have been part of the AI data centre race.

US President Donald Trump on Friday reiterated his supported for what he calls "super intelligence", saying only "foolish leadership" would "say no to the riches they bring".

However, there have also been concerns over whether the enormous amounts of money being spent on AI will pay off.

Russ Shaw, founder of global tech advocacy firm Tech London Advocates, said the election result was sending a message that a rethink was needed on AI.

"The incoming Congress is going to really focus on AI in a very dramatic way," he told the BBC's Business Today.

"I'm a big fan of AI, but I'm watching what these companies are doing, and they're not communicating effectively at all, particularly in the US, about what the benefits of AI are all about."

Pierre Baqué, chief executive of AI platform Neural Concept, said the share movements were a "necessary market correction" that reflected a legitimate concern about the amount of money being poured into AI infrastructure.

"The industry must move beyond unchecked infrastructure investment and demonstrate greater financial discipline," he said.

"We are entering a critical transition phase, a market purgatory where raw tech must prove its widespread economic value."

Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said it had been a brutal week for markets, and the key question was whether the jump in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq would be sustained.

"Once investors have had the weekend to catch their breath, next week could give a clearer indication of whether the tech trade is going down the pan or fighting back."

Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck

As well as the fallout of the midterms and the plunge in artificial intelligence stocks, US traders will also be digesting the latest jobs figures.

And those numbers were better than expected: US employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, well above the average monthly increase and more than double what analysts had expected.

Overall the unemployment rate, which counts the number of people who are out of work but actively looking for a job, eased slightly to 4.1% from 4.2% in September .

The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the unemployment rate has remained in the narrow range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March.

Neil Birrell, chief investment officer at investment firm Premier Miton, said while the jobs figures may feel like second billing to the market movements they were still important.

"The US economy is running hard which may mean the risks the markets are worrying about at the moment are not such a risk to the real economy as is being feared," he said.

items.title: Trump ha nominato Stephen Miller capo di gabinetto della Casa Bianca
items.content:
In un post sulla sua piattaforma social Truth, il presidente degli Stati Uniti Donald Trump ha annunciato la nomina di Stephen Miller a capo di gabinetto (chief of staff) della Casa Bianca. Miller, che finora era vicecapo di gabinetto, sostituirà Susie Wiles , che aveva questo incarico dal 2025, dopo essere stata la stratega e la responsabile della campagna presidenziale di Trump. Wiles aveva presentato le proprie dimissioni a Trump giovedì sera, dopo la gravissima sconfitta dei Repubblicani alle elezioni di metà mandato.

Miller, che da molto tempo è una delle persone più vicine a Trump, è noto, tra le altre cose, per aver pianificato e messo in atto il programma sulle politiche migratorie portato avanti da Trump, anche nelle sue misure più estreme.

Quello di capo di gabinetto è il ruolo di maggiore potere fra quelli che non prevedono un’elezione (e nemmeno un voto di conferma del Senato). Il capo di gabinetto gestisce un enorme staff politico e operativo e ha un ruolo centrale nel definire le strategie della Casa Bianca, dalle leggi da discutere e approvare alla comunicazione dell’attività di governo. Decide le priorità politiche e organizza la gestione delle crisi internazionali. Il ruolo potenzialmente più critico è però quello di “filtro”: stabilisce quali decisioni devono essere prese personalmente dal presidente e quali possono essere delegate, oltre ad avere l’ultima parola su chi debba incontrare.

items.title: A Jev that can ask Opus for help gives Opus accuracy at 4x lower cost
items.summary: Article URL: https://hightouch.com/blog/llm-judges-identity-resolution Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50397429 Points: 531 # Comments: 128
items.content:
We wanted to test whether LLMs and decision models, specifically Jev and Luna, could solve a hard problem that we encounter regularly (grading identity resolution results). We found that while both models performed okay out of the box (88.8–97.3% accuracy), implementing a hybrid model that combines Jev + Opus achieves frontier accuracy at > 4x lower costs.

Identity resolution is the process of mapping data to corresponding real people. More precisely, say you have a set of data records D . Determine a set of identities I and mapping m(D)->I such that each record d ∈ D maps to an identity i ∈ I , each i corresponds to exactly one real person in the real world, and no two i correspond to the same person in the real world.

This is foundational for any company wishing to do outreach, personalization, or analytics on customers. You can’t know, for instance, the lifetime value of a customer without being able to map all their purchases to a single identity.

For example, the input data might contain the following records. IDR would ideally create one identity, Alice , and associate all of these records with Alice .

In practice, IDR is very difficult. People share emails, move addresses, etc. There might also be errors in the data. See some examples here:

The most common and problematic issue with IDR is over-merging . This is when an identity i incorrectly corresponds to multiple people in the real world.

On real data, there is no answer key we can consult after we’ve merged records into identities. If there were, then we'd just use that to match data, and we wouldn't need to do IDR. This makes it very difficult to assess the accuracy of any IDR algorithm. In practice, teams will spend months attempting to determine if their IDR is working.

You can use heuristics to look for statistical signs of over-merged profiles (count the number of emails per identity, etc), but ultimately you need to sample output identities and review them by hand to know how well your IDR algorithm is performing.

To do this, we define the records Dᵢ as the set of d such that m(d) -> i for any given i . If the IDR engine is successful, then we should only find evidence of one real person in any given Dᵢ .

Human sampling is slow (~50 identities/hr), and sampling small numbers of identities gives poor estimates of over-merging. Over-merges are rare in a healthy graph, and estimating a rare rate precisely takes more samples than people expect (> 1000 samples to get the error down to under +-1% on over-merging rate)

An LLM should, intuitively, be able to replicate what a human is doing when they inspect an identity. If a model can judge identities at human accuracy, then we could spin up as many LLMs as we want to grade identities in parallel. A sample of 100,000 identities could be evaluated in seconds. This would enable much faster iteration cycles when setting up IDR, and make maintenance much easier.

Of particular interest are Jev and GPT-6 Luna . These are members of a new class of language models that return a 0-1 confidence score that a specific condition is true. They are far faster and cheaper than current frontier models.

We made a benchmark with pseudopeople , a tool from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation at the University of Washington. It simulates a fictional US town and generates records of its residents from multiple sources. We also added a bunch of realistic data errors.

From those records, we built 1,000 identities. Half are one person with noisy records, and half are over-merges. Then we spun up some models and measured how they did.

Then we described the kinds of noise in the data, so that a typo would not be mistaken for a new person:

Every model gained the most from the error examples. The data context then added at most a point for the frontier models and wasn't helpful for the decision models. Our guess is that decision models don't really reason, so providing fundamental context doesn't help them. We kept the full prompt for all models to keep things consistent. With the final prompt, the results were:

Initially, we used a 50% confidence threshold, but this was arbitrary. We can adjust it to trade one type of error for another.

The cutoff matters a lot for Jev and very little for Luna. We settled on 60% for Jev and 70% for Luna, which maximize accuracy in each case. Here’s how both models perform with a better-calibrated threshold.

So far Luna looks very good; indeed, it's surprisingly close to the frontier models at a small fraction of their cost. We decided to up the difficulty of our test to see if the frontier models could pull ahead.

We used the same town and the same kinds of noise, but only tricky cases. We tried to trick the model by constructing cases including:

Great, there's a clear gap between the frontier models and Luna now. Interestingly, Luna is also now level with Jev, despite being ahead previously. We started digging into the cases where Luna and Jev got it wrong to see whether we could improve accuracy without paying for a frontier model.

In investigating the cases in which Jev and Luna missed while the larger models got it right, we noticed a very interesting pattern. Let's start with the easier dataset to see it clearly.

Most of Jev's mistakes are closer to 50% confidence, which is what you'd expect out of a well-calibrated model. Luna, on the other hand, seems quite overconfident in the 90–100% bucket despite making far fewer mistakes.

Let's see what happens when we re-run on the trickier cases.

While Jev's confidence incorrectly shifts higher, its calibration remains far better than Luna's. Luna starts to be spectacularly over-confident here that it has identified an over-merge.

All that matters is that we can, on average, cheaply judge whether an identity is over-merged. We don't have to only rely on one model. If the cheap model is well calibrated, we can forward a small portion of our identities to an expensive model for a second opinion.

Given how overconfident Luna is, we can guess that it won't help Luna as much, but Jev should really be able to take advantage of this.

Not only does this approach bring Jev past Luna in accuracy, but it also almost meets the accuracy of Opus alone. Granted, it’s more expensive than hybrid Luna for pretty similar performance.

Now the gap is very clear. Hybrid Jev's better confidence calibration means it elegantly sends more cases to Opus on harder data without any harness or prompting change. We pay more, but it's a system that will automatically scale spend when needed to maintain accuracy, which is what we want. It's also still way cheaper than Opus alone. While Luna appears to do better out of the box, its overconfidence condemns it to mediocre performance in the hybrid model.

Calibration matters! Whereas Luna works better out of the box, its overconfidence prevents success on harder datasets. The hybrid approach is clearly useful, and we suspect it's not just useful in this domain.

Hybrid Jev's ability to handle arbitrary problem difficulty is very valuable. You never know how tricky the identities are going to be in practice, so a system that will dynamically flex to spend more when it needs to is awesome.

If we were more cost-sensitive or knew the cases judged were easier, we might pick hybrid Luna, but we think hybrid Jev's advantages are worth the additional costs. We could adjust our thresholds to send fewer cases for a second opinion to bring down costs at the cost of a bit of accuracy in the hybrid Jev approach.

In future posts we'll discuss how we think about under-merging, and look at how performance degrades if we go to open-weight decision models vs. relying on proprietary APIs.

Test data generated with pseudopeople ; no real people appear in any example. Model costs and latencies are what we observed in our own setup and will vary.

items.title: Firecracker VM Escape: PwnEscape Part 2
items.summary: Article URL: https://pwn.ai/blog/firecracker-escape Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50397219 Points: 260 # Comments: 112
items.content:
Firecracker is supposed to keep untrusted code inside a microVM. We escaped it and achieved code execution as root on the host.

We found how it saved registers, changed where it would resume, and made it execute a call of our choosing when it returned from KVM. The guest then restored the temporary stack changes. Firecracker kept running, and the VM remained accessible over SSH.

PwnEscape Part 1 introduced the host memory primitive behind this work. Here we follow the next part of the chain: using that access to find Firecracker in memory and take over a live thread from inside the guest. This is a continuation to show CVE-2026-99999 on a Firecracker setup.

A Firecracker microVM has a process on the host that manages it. Each virtual CPU, or vCPU, has a thread in that process. The thread enters KVM to run the guest and returns to Firecracker when an event needs handling in userspace. Firecracker documents this arrangement in its architecture overview .

While the thread is in that system call, the host kernel holds its saved userspace registers in a structure called pt_regs . These registers describe the Firecracker thread: its instruction pointer says where execution should resume, and its stack pointer says which userspace stack it should use.

That made the return from KVM_RUN an attractive target. If we could locate and modify the saved frame, we could choose the code Firecracker executed when the thread returned to userspace. A guest operation that caused such a return would provide the trigger.

We already had access to selected host physical memory through a guest mapping. To use it, we needed to identify the Firecracker process, find code we could call in that process, and locate the register frame belonging to its active vCPU thread. The starting point was a page of memory we controlled inside the guest.

Figure 1. The guest identifies its Firecracker process, finds the saved registers for a vCPU thread, and redirects the thread when it returns from KVM.

The guest and host use different physical address spaces. A page has a guest physical address, or GPA, inside the VM and a host physical address, or HPA, in the machine backing it. On the target, Extended Page Tables (EPT) provide the translation between them.

We placed a recognizable byte pattern, a nonce, in a guest page. The first resolver took that page's known GPA and its contents as inputs. Together, they gave us an address to translate and a way to check whether the translation reached our page.

The resolver searched the host physical ranges covered by the memory primitive for candidate EPT roots. An EPT root is the starting point of the translation tables. For each candidate, the resolver followed the entries selected by the guest address until it reached a physical page, then checked that page for the nonce.

The snippets below are explanatory pseudocode with descriptive helper names. They show the data passed between stages and the checks used to connect them.

The nonce check connected a proposed translation to memory we controlled. The broader search produced two candidates; validation of the nested page tables reduced them to one EPT root. Walking that root gave us the host physical address of our guest page.

We called this result guest_page_hpa and passed it to the next resolver. We now had a recognizable object in host memory. The next task was finding the host process that mapped it.

Firecracker maps memory used by the guest into its own address space. That mapping gave us a way to work backward from the guest page to the process.

Host processes use page tables to translate their virtual addresses into physical memory. The top level is called the page global directory, or PGD. Recovering the appropriate PGD would let us translate addresses inside Firecracker and read its code and stack through the memory primitive.

Our reverse mapper searched the native host page tables for a mapping of guest_page_hpa . A normal page table walk starts with a virtual address and produces a physical address. Here, we looked for a mapping to a physical page we already knew, then recovered the virtual address and page table root associated with it.

This connected the host process's virtual mapping to the physical page found through EPT. The reverse mapper returned one validated address space. We retained its root as host_pgd and used it to inspect the process.

The next resolver looked for the Firecracker executable in those mappings. It identified an ELF image and checked a known byte sequence in Firecracker's write(2) wrapper. That connected the recovered address space to the binary we were targeting.

ASLR changes where an executable is loaded. The difference between an address in the ELF image and its corresponding runtime address is the load bias. Once the mapper had identified the image, it could recover that bias and use it to locate the code required by the exploit:

The mapper returned the load bias as firecracker_base . With that value and host_pgd , we could locate code in the running process, translate its virtual address to host physical memory, and compare the bytes there with the expected binary.

We checked three locations: the write(2) wrapper that would produce our proof, the continuation after the KVM ioctl, and a short xor eax,eax; ret sequence needed to return cleanly. Their purposes become relevant when we construct the return path below.

At this point, the guest could inspect the Firecracker image and its private mappings. We still needed the saved registers of the thread currently running our VM.

Figure 2. The nonce identifies the guest page in host memory. Its mapping leads to a host page table root, which lets the next resolver locate and validate the Firecracker image.

The frame finder took host_pgd and firecracker_base from the preceding stages. It used them to recognize the host thread's saved state.

The most useful clue was the return address. A vCPU thread in KVM_RUN should have a saved instruction pointer at the corresponding ioctl continuation in Firecracker. We could calculate that address from the validated binary and its load bias.

We then searched host memory for a pt_regs frame consistent with that call. An address match alone would also pick up stale stack contents, so the candidate had to satisfy several related checks:

The stack check tied the frame to the same address space we had recovered from the guest page. The instruction and caller addresses tied it to the Firecracker image. The syscall fields tied it to the operation running the vCPU.

The search left one candidate. Its location was stored as frame_hpa , the host physical address of the saved register frame. We passed it, the PGD, and the load bias to the final helper.

Before changing memory, the helper repeated the code signature, frame, and stack checks. This ensured that the active stage used the same process state the resolvers had identified. The subsequent execution and recovery checks would establish that the selected frame was live.

Figure 3. The candidate register frame must agree with the KVM ioctl, the recovered process page tables, and the validated Firecracker code.

We chose a simple payload: make the Firecracker process write a recognizable string to its own stderr. This would give the host runner an observable result from the process we had taken over.

The string was N8V23M2\n , seven characters followed by a newline. It occupies eight bytes and fits in one stack word. The call we wanted Firecracker to execute was:

Here 2 is Firecracker's stderr file descriptor. The buffer pointer must refer to the string in Firecracker's address space, so we stored the string on its private userspace stack.

We saved three stack words before modifying them. One held the string; the other two held the return addresses for the temporary call sequence. We then changed the saved register frame to supply the wrapper address, its arguments, and a stack pointer for that sequence:

Returning from write also needed care. A successful write of eight bytes returns 8 , while a successful KVM_RUN call returns zero . We placed the address of xor eax,eax; ret first in the return sequence. It clears the return value before the second address brings execution back to Firecracker's original ioctl continuation.

With the stack and saved registers prepared, the guest wrote one byte to its serial port. That operation caused the vCPU thread to return from KVM_RUN . The kernel restored the modified registers, and Firecracker entered the write wrapper with our arguments.

The wrapper emitted the marker, the return sequence cleared eax , and the thread rejoined its original execution path. After control returned to the guest, the helper restored all three stack words.

Figure 4. The saved register frame enters the write wrapper. Two return addresses lead through the return-value adjustment and back into the original Firecracker path.

The host runner captured Firecracker's stderr separately from the guest. The complete output was:

The capture contained exactly eight bytes, including the final newline. Firecracker was still running, guest SSH was responsive, and the helper had restored the three temporary stack words.
